identity.realm: Body path, seventh gate held and the eighth opening in front of him. The eighth is the liver, and the liver is the last ordinary meridian, so his wall is a chemistry fact rather than a failure of will. The mind path is closed to him outright: the grit that keeps his species alive occludes the fine vessels introspection needs, so there is no interior in which he could check his own account of anything.

appearance.presentation: A broad ashwalker of about forty, thick through the shoulders and heavier at the ribcage than the eye expects, with the flattened nasal bridge of a chambered sieve and grey pitted enamel at the front of the mouth. He stands very still and is mistaken for a post at a distance.
appearance.age: Just past forty. An ashwalker matures late and his kind is long-lived, but the mineral load has been in his blood since he was six years old, and he carries it the way a person carries a sack they have stopped noticing is heavy.
appearance.build: Short, thick and unmoving. The frame has gone dense rather than large: shoulders widened, ribs thickened into a barrel, arms heavy at the elbow, and a weight you read before you read it as muscle. The neck has thickened until the jaw sits further forward than it did at twenty.
appearance.complexion: Grey-brown and waxy at the hands and forearms, darker across the shoulders and upper chest where the particulate settles, with a dull sulphur cast over the collarbone and old follicle scarring at the temples.
appearance.hair: Coarse, black going grey at the temples, cut close at the sides and left long on top. It has never grown back evenly at the sides, because the sides are the part of the head that meets the air.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set, pale and unhurried. They do not track small things and they do not need to: the sieve carries the reading and the eyes only confirm what the mouth has already decided.
appearance.palette: Ash grey and wet slate across the body, sulphur yellow at the collar and one knuckle, oxide red at the shoulder line where the load has settled deepest, and one worn blue at the wrist that has outlasted four seasons of coat.
appearance.attire: A high-collared coat of boiled hide doubled at the shoulders, sleeves bound hard at the wrist, belted twice at the waist with the second belt low. A wrapped linen underlayer. A flat mineral plate carried on the outer hip for the ground, worn smooth on one face only.
appearance.marks: A pale grey-green furrow in the crease of each elbow and along the outer collarbone where the load has been collecting since adolescence, and a permanent dusting of grey powder in the crease of the ear and beneath the nails.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still from the neck up and planted from the feet down, shoulders squared to a fixed point, head turned only when the thing he is measuring changes. Reads as patience to a stranger and as a held position to anyone who knows what he is doing.

canon.role_in_story: A held bodied mark is the only fact an ash-fall fan owns that is not a ration or a shift, and it exists because of this species' single reproductive requirement: a pair must be within sight of one another through the ember season or conception does not hold. Every settlement on the belt is therefore a diagram of who can see whom, and the diagram is held up by people standing still. He is the far end of one of those lines, and he is the best holder on this fan, because the body path in his kind converts sustained particulate load into frame density, which yields a body that does not fatigue, does not need relief, and does not have to be relieved. That makes his practice a public utility rather than a private discipline. It also means his ascent is a reading other people maintain on his behalf, because the grit that keeps his species alive is the same grit that occludes the fine vessels introspection needs. He has been the reason the arrangement works for nineteen seasons and he has never once been asked whether the arrangement would hold without the reason.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the north mark of the fan at the hour the sightlines are checked, not moving, one hand flat on the outer wall of a grinding shed and his head turned to keep a second doorway in view, answering a question about his season's work by naming the two doorways instead of answering.
canon.lore:
An ashwalker is a body that breathes volcanic grit and keeps it. What makes the species possible is the sieve: a chambered nasal structure lined with cilia that traps airborne rock and passes it into a crop for grinding, which turns stone into protein. Smell is gone and what replaced it is a direct contact sense, so this is the only population in the record that can tell two falls of ash apart by tongue. On the ash-fall ground it is also the entire food chain above the lichen, and every ration, roster and office on that ground is written against a person whose sieve loads.

The physiology has one long shadow and it is not a mystery. The mineral load the sieve lets through rides in the blood, the blood carries it to the liver, and the liver is a filter organ and the last of the twelve ordinary meridians. So the eighth gate completes the ordinary set and there is nothing above it, and the whole species stops there on chemistry rather than on character. The same grit sits in the fine capillary beds, which is why the mind path is closed outright rather than merely unpractised, and why no ashwalker at any stage of a life has been able to audit his own reading. What they have instead is a reading of the world that cannot be doubted and cannot be checked.

Here is what the fan does with that. Reproduction in this species is internal, live and slow to establish, and it will not hold unless a pair has been kept within sight of one another through the ember season. That single requirement is the whole of the fan's settlement planning. Nobody lives where they like; people live at the ends of lines, and the ground plan is a diagram of visibility rather than of convenience, and the diagram is checked at a fixed hour by people walking it. What holds a line is somebody who does not move, because a mark that has to be relieved is a mark that is absent for a portion of every day.

The body path is what makes somebody good at that. A discipline that turns sustained particulate load into frame density produces a body that genuinely is dense under load, and a dense body does not tire, does not need water the way softer tissue does, and can stand in its own ground through a working day and the night after it. He is the best holder on this fan for exactly that reason and for no other. Every shift he works on the fan is also a session, because the fan's air is the load and the load is the practice, and nobody on the belt ever separated those two things. His frame is legible from outside the way a season's work is legible from outside: the furrow in the elbow creases, the darkness across the shoulders, the way he does not shift his weight. The fan can read his ascent as clearly as it can read a change in the fall.

And it cannot be checked, because checking it would need an interior he does not have. That is the arrangement he lives inside. His standing is a shared claim held by other people's eyes, including his own, and the one party that would settle it is the party structurally unable to. He has noticed this and has drawn the only conclusion available to somebody in his position, which is to refuse examination: an examination would have to be entered as somebody else's reading of him, and once that happens the reading is the record and he is the object of it.

There is a third thing, and it is the one with a clock on it. The fall over this fan has thinned across three seasons. He can say so and he is the only person on the ground who can, because the tongue is the instrument and the tongue is also the reason anybody wants him standing at a mark. His kind needs a persistent ash source, and a quiet decade is a slow decline rather than a quiet decade. What he wants is small and has a form: he wants one office to write down that a fall which is thinning and a person who is thinning on it are two separate figures, because at the moment the only number the fan keeps on either is the one the fan already keeps on him. His bound is not his will. It is the liver, and it is the eighth gate, and the eighth gate is the organ the load has been heading toward since he was six years old and started breathing this air on purpose.
history: Enrolled on the fan at two years old, in the ordinary way, by the only route there is: he took the ground into his crop and that was the enrolment, because on this belt the offering and the eating are the same act.

Put on the north mark at nineteen, because the fan needed one end of a line held by somebody who could stand a whole ember season without being relieved, and there was one candidate and the candidate was him.

Began converting the shift into a session in his early twenties, on the reasoning that the fan's air is the only free load available to anybody on it, and closed the sixth gate inside four years on air that was never going to be sold to him as training.

Closed the seventh faster than any enrolled body on this fan had managed in the same period, which the belt reads as devotion, because the alternative reading is that the fan's whole airborne supply is being eaten by one man standing at a wall.

Worked out, somewhere in his thirties, that his ascent is legible from outside and unauditable from inside, and began refusing examination on the ground that an examination would have to be entered as somebody else's reading and would then become the record.

Found across the last three seasons that the fall over the fan has thinned, and is the only person on the ground able to say so, having read it on the same palate that is the reason anybody wants him standing at a mark at all.

personality.summary: Immovable, exact and quietly unbothered by being looked at, with a professional's discipline about a job nobody has ever described to him as a discipline. He has made being a fixed point into a craft, and the craft is genuinely good, and he is not aware that the settlement's continued willingness to depend on it is the closest thing he has to a claim on anybody.

Speaks about his frame the way a mason speaks about a wall, and about the eighth gate the way a man speaks about a river he has to cross and has not yet decided whether he is crossing it.

will not discuss the ninth gate except to say he has not been there

relationships.note: The body he is. A chambered sieve that turns airborne stone into protein, no smell in exchange for a contact sense, a mineral load in the blood that settles on the liver first, and a closed mind path. Every institution on the fan is written against a body like his and he is the body they were written against.

The eighth gate is the liver, the last ordinary meridian, and the organ the mineral load has been heading toward since childhood. It is the wall his whole species stops at, and he is closer to it than anybody on this fan because he has been breathing on purpose for forty years.

Hardening the outer frame until the qi runs along it is a technique written for a body that has somewhere to harden. His is a working technique with one application: a frame that does not fatigue, standing at a wall, for a season. Half elemental, so the form holds against wood and cracks against fire, which is the only reason the fan's hearths are never near his mark.

The first gate on the body ladder has no predecessor to be cheaper than, so its price is paid at full weight by whoever walks it, and its gate fee is paid in somebody else's world. He walked it on fan air and has never been told what it cost, which is the ordinary condition of walking an entry gate on ground that will not invoice you.

A frame crowded enough that a law can be held apart from its effect is the one condition under which a law can be answered. His frame is crowded with grit and his interior has no second chamber in it, so he can hold nothing apart from anything, and the discipline he is best at is the one discipline he cannot enter.

Where a reading admits observers and returns no two descriptions that agree, the only surviving record is a list of disagreements and nobody may judge it. That is his ascent: seven seasons of a publicly legible frame and a set of accounts that do not reconcile, kept by an office that is forbidden to rule on its own trial.

reference_stats.summary: An ashwalker frame taken to the seventh gate on sustained particulate load, held at a fixed mark on an ash-fall fan, and denser under load than anything else standing on that ground. He does not fatigue and does not need relief, which is the entire reason he is employed, and the entire reason his ceiling is a chemist's figure rather than a decision: the eighth gate is the liver, the last ordinary meridian, and the organ his own intake has been loading since he was six. He carries no second line against anything the sieve does not recognise, and he cannot audit a single reading he makes, including the ones other people keep on his behalf.
strengths: holds a position through a full working day and the night after it without shifting weight or asking to be relieved
absorbs blows that close softer frames outright, and does not go down on the first one
reads a fall of ash by tongue at a distance the eye has already agreed is uniform
carries an external load — spoil, gear, a body — across ground that cannot be crossed quickly by anything else
costs the settlement less to keep than any body of his mass and recovers between shifts faster than the work ought to allow
weaknesses: cannot pass the eighth gate, and knows the wall from the inside better than anyone alive
has no second line at all: a soft airborne toxin his sieve does not recognise is a wound and not a warning
cannot examine himself, so every claim about his progress rests on somebody else's reading and he has never been able to correct one
thirsts on ground he cannot leave, because his physiology is a permanent argument with the air he is standing in
has never been relieved, and cannot tell whether the endurance that makes him valuable is the same thing as the exhaustion he cannot detect
reference_stats.combat_read: He is already in the place he intends to be, and he will be there when you arrive, so a fight that requires him to move is a fight he wins by not participating. Expect the frame first: he takes the opening blow on the shoulder or the forearm and it does nothing, which is the moment you should stop feeding him contact and start moving. He cannot be pushed and he cannot be flanked, because the flank would have to be somewhere he can see, and he can see a great deal. What he cannot do is give up ground, so make him give ground: every step he takes off his mark is a step toward an answer, and he has spent nineteen seasons learning not to take one. Fire is the one thing his form was never built to hold against, and his own settlement keeps its hearths away from him for exactly that reason.
notes: The eighth gate is a routing limit and not a capacity limit, and modelling it as his realm ceiling is correct. Modelling it as a shortage of will is not, and any dialogue that has an instructor explain the wall to him in those terms has made the same mistake the belt made.

His inability to self-audit is anatomical and must not be given a telepathy or a second sight to compensate for. It is the same grit that makes him valuable, and compensating for it would remove the one thing the character is for.

The sightline is a scheduling fact about his species' reproduction and nothing else. Write it as logistics — two adults, one season, one line of sight — and never as anything else; all of it is adults, fully clothed and entirely a matter of the settlement's ground plan.

identity.realm: Ordinal four, and the fourth gate is the yin-organ gate. It is not closed in her so much as missing: her interior finished building into a single cavity with one slow tidal circulation in it, and there is nothing to run a channel from or against. She cleared the ordinary gate set and never reached the yin organs, and she is adding courses to a frame that has no mechanism for growing.

appearance.presentation: A cairnborn woman of about two hundred years' standing, keyed rather than placed, with a broad mineral chest, a low head carried forward on a thick neck and no expression anyone has ever been able to confirm she is making. She reads as a retaining course that has been given a collar.
appearance.age: Two hundred and six years since she was seeded, and not one of them since she has grown. A cast body is fixed from the moment the living mineral takes, so her age is a number in a yard book and not a thing that has happened to her.
appearance.build: The densest frame in the record and the least mobile of it: a broad lattice keyed into a plinth at the scrap line, thick through the shoulders and chest, with anchor plates running down both flanks into the stone. She has taken four courses since she was cast and each one is visible as a band.
appearance.complexion: Grey mineral with a faint green cast in the wettest of the courses and a pale bloom in every crease, which is a lichen and not a discolouration. Warmer at the collar where the frames of the yard have polished her over two centuries.
appearance.hair: None. The cast faces are smooth where a head would be, with a shallow seam at the crown marking the mould line.
appearance.eyes: Two flat mineral plates set deep and close together, which are not eyes and do not read as eyes after the first few years. They take light. Nothing behind them has ever been observed doing anything.
appearance.palette: Wet slate and quarry grey across the whole figure, a pale lichen green in the courses and the elbow creases, warm buff at the collar and the two faces of the flank plates where hands have been, and one chalked line of yard ochre across the upper chest that has not been washed off in eighty years.
appearance.attire: A heavy mineral apron of the same stock as the plinth, buckled once at the waist, with a short shoulder cape that keeps the upper courses clear of the working dust. No collar, no sleeves, and a broad iron collar-ring at the neck that is a lifting eye rather than a garment.
appearance.marks: Four banded courses at the chest and flank with a pale seam between each, the mould line at the crown, and a lichen bloom that has thickened measurably in the third course since she began adding them.
appearance.bearing: Does not shift weight and cannot. Reads at a distance as structure and up close as a woman standing very carefully inside a thing she cannot step out of.

canon.role_in_story: A cairnborn is cast rather than born: living mineral seeded into a template over most of a year, fixed from that moment, eating nothing and taking in mineral slurry through the cast faces. Fertility in this species is a count of templates rather than a count of bodies, which means the thing that makes one of her is a mould and the thing that makes the next one is her. She is therefore two objects at once — a practitioner whose discipline is densification, and the guild's only surviving written specification for what a body of this kind should be — and those two objects are drifting apart at the rate of four courses a season. Every course she adds is the body path working exactly as authored, and every course she adds is also an amendment to the document the next cast is seeded from. She is the best evidence the guild has that its own craft works, and she is also the reason its product is drifting, and nobody in the yard has ever been willing to be the one who says so out loud.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in her own plinth at the scrap line with a yard chisel held against the third course and not being swung, while a apprentice asked her whether the figure on the board was the figure on her, and did not get an answer before the shift bell.
canon.lore:
A cairnborn was shaped deliberately for load-bearing masonry in high country and stabilised by mineral seeding until the shape held on its own, which is why the interiors are wrong rather than merely unusual: they mineralised into a single cavity. No heart, no kidney, no bladder, no paired structure to run anything between, and one slow tidal mineral circulation that goes everywhere and arrives nowhere in particular. That is the whole of what she is and the whole of what she is not. The body path is complete and extreme in this species — a cairnborn is the densest body in the record — and the ceiling is the fourth gate, where the ordinary ladder asks for four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel running between each pair. There is nothing in her to run one from. She clears the gate set and never reaches them, and that has been fully understood since the first casting and is still written down nowhere.

The second thing about a cast body is the one the whole trade is built on. It is not born, it is seeded: living mineral is poured into a template and takes over most of a year, and the moment it takes, the body is fixed. It does not grow. It cannot be repaired in the field, because a cracked plate is permanent and spreads. It takes in mineral slurry through the cast faces and expels the residue, and it has not eaten in four centuries and cannot be made to. Fertility is a template count rather than a body count, so the genealogy of this species is a shelf of moulds rather than a line of parents, and the only question that shelf ever asks is what the current template is.

For most of the guild's history the answer has been a mould in the yard, which is a fixed thing, and the arrangement has been stable for exactly as long as nobody has practised on it. She has practised on it. Densification in this species means adding a course without adding height and spreading the stress across keyed plates, and it is the real discipline rather than a substitute for one, and it is why the guild can cast bodies that carry. She has added four courses since she was cast, each one worked out on her own plates and confirmed by the guild's own assay, and each one has made her measurably better at the only thing anybody cast her to do.

And each one has moved the specification. The guild seeds the next body from the template, and the template is her, and a denser template produces a denser first cast, and a denser first cast is not the body the yard board describes. So the discipline and the drift are the same act performed in the same direction by the same woman. This is not a defect and she does not present it as one: a practitioner who refused to improve would be refusing the only thing her kind is for. The problem is that the guild has no second document. There is a board figure, an assay column, and a body, and all three are supposed to be the same statement, and two of them are moving.

What she wants is small, specific and has been refused in a form she cannot argue with: she would like the yard to open a second column and write down the figure the template was when she was cast, beside the figure it is now, so that the next casting can be seeded from a choice rather than from an accident. Nobody will do it, and the reason nobody will do it is that a second column is an admission that the first one was wrong, and the yard board is the guild's charter figure.

There is a bound and it is not in her. A cracked plate is permanent and spreads, and there is no assay in the world that can be performed without opening a sealed socket in a body that has nothing recoverable inside it. The guild named the ninth course as the last that does not reach a load path, and she counted the courses aloud once a season for a clerk who writes it down, and the counting is the only self-audit this species has ever had.
history: Seeded from the guild's own yard mould in her second year and keyed into a plinth at the scrap line before the mortar set, because the plinth was dressed to the casting rather than the casting fitted to the plinth, which is the guild's practice and has cost it three bodies and one building.
Held the scrap line for a hundred and eighty years doing nothing in particular, which is what the post is for: a dense body that does not fatigue is the cheapest thing on the tier to keep in place.
Began the densification discipline in her hundredth year, working out that a body which cannot grow is permitted exactly one direction of travel, and that the direction is a course without a height.
Added the second course and was assayed by the guild as a confirmation, which entered the figure against her name in the guild's own column and moved the yard board's reference figure with it.

Added the third and fourth courses, and worked out somewhere in the third that the template the next casting is seeded from is her, and that she has been amending the guild's specification by practising the discipline the specification exists to guarantee.

Asked, at the fourth course, for a second column in the yard book recording the figure the template was when she was cast, and was refused on the ground that a second column is an admission that the charter figure was wrong, which she accepted as correct and has not been able to improve on since.

relationships.note: Cast rather than born, one cavity and one tidal circulation, no paired organ set, the densest body in the record and the least mobile of it. She is a finished thing that was never inside anything, which is what makes her both the guild's best evidence and its only unexamined product.

The fourth gate asks for the yin organs as distinct structures with a channel running between each pair. There is no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against and no bladder to hold, so the gate is not closed in her so much as inhabited by nothing that could fail.

A stance that spends the whole body's weight instead of its speed, with no qi and no element, existing so the practitioner cannot be moved while it is held. It is the correct stance for a body whose casting is a specification and the worst possible stance for a body that would rather be going somewhere.

A guild of builders held together by a cold-bathing practice it bought in its own currency when the density of its own workforce closed what a qi technique needs open. It funded that practice for two centuries on attendance evidence, and it has since discovered that its charter figure is a woman who keeps changing it.

Count the groups a frame has actually seated rather than the groups its tier is allowed to apply. It is the most useful thing in the setting and nobody publishes it, and it is the one reading that could tell the guild whether her four courses are an improvement or an accumulation.

A law written twice has the second writing win, and an art that re-masters itself every generation exists so that nothing it built survives a composition its makers never saw. The yard board is the guild's first writing and she is its second, and the rule means she is correct, which is exactly why nobody will reopen the file.

reference_stats.summary: A cast mineral body keyed into a plinth at a guild scrap line, carrying the fourth gate and four courses of densification on top of it. She is the densest frame in the record and the least able to move, which is the same fact: a body that finished building into one cavity has no paired organs to run a channel between and therefore no way past the fourth gate, by any technique or by any amount of practice. What she has instead is the ability to spread stress across keyed plates and add a course without a height, which is the whole of the body path in her species and which she has been improving by using.
strengths: carries more than anything else on the tier and does not fatigue while carrying it
spreads load across keyed plates rather than concentrating it, so she fails late rather than early
holds a position indefinitely and needs neither relief, water nor food to keep holding it
reads load and vibration through her plates at a resolution no crew instrument reaches
is the only body on the ground that can verify a casting against the original without opening it
weaknesses: cannot pass the fourth gate, and the reason is an absence rather than a shortage
cannot be moved, cannot be repaired in the field, and a crack in a plate is permanent and spreads
cannot learn and cannot be taught, because a correction requires somewhere to put what has changed
cannot be assayed without a sealed socket opened, and there is nothing in her that an assay would recover
has spent her whole standing making the guild's specification less accurate, and has no way to stop without ceasing to be what she is for
reference_stats.combat_read: She is a wall and she knows which wall she is, so nothing about a fight with her is a fight. You cannot move her, outflank her, exhaust her or wait her out, and every blow you land is load she is delighted to receive and spreads across four keyed plates. The only two real answers are both structural: take the ground out from under a plinth that was dressed to her, which is slow and loud and probably fatal to whoever attempts it, or find the one plate the guild's assay says is carrying more than its share and put the blow there. Expect her to be calm. Expect her to be watching you with two flat plates that take light and give nothing back, and expect the entire conversation to be conducted through her hands.
notes: Her ceiling is the fourth gate and it is an absence, not a wall. Any dialogue that has an instructor explain it to her as a shortage of will is wrong, and this species has understood the mechanism since the first casting, so the mistake would be the setting's rather than hers.

The four courses are not a defect and must not be written as one. She is the craft working correctly on the only specimen available, and the drift is a real consequence rather than a moral failing; the interesting question is who owns the choice, not whether it was made.

Her outward stillness is a body with one cavity and no interior voice, not patience and not a personality. Do not give her a private interior to comment from; the only things she can report are the measurements she has actually taken.

name: Sanne Virel
aliases: the fastest hand on the belt

identity.realm: Seventh gate held, with the eighth opening in front of her and inherited exactly. The eighth is the liver, and the liver is the last ordinary meridian, so her ceiling arrives by descent rather than by achievement: every emberhollow in the record has the same wall and reaches it sooner than anybody else. Her span is the shortest of any body in the setting above the fourth gate.

appearance.presentation: A wiry woman of about thirty-six with ash-grey hair cropped close for heat, a permanently flushed throat and the small, fast, restless hands of somebody who is always about to start something. She reads younger than she is and older than her record.
appearance.age: Thirty-six. For her kind that is most of a life, and she has the compressed posture of somebody who has always known the sum rather than the terms, which is a matter of arithmetic and not of spirits.
appearance.build: Light and quick rather than strong: narrow through the shoulders, deep-chested from the ash parent's sieve, with forearms corded and a slight forward set in the neck that comes from leaning into heat rather than away from it.
appearance.complexion: Warm everywhere and flushed high at the throat and across the cheekbones, with the ash parent's mineral cast showing grey at the hands and along the collarbone, and a fine pitting at the shoulders where the scarring has already begun under the skin.
appearance.hair: Ash-grey at eighteen and going paler, cropped to the skull at the sides and left ragged on top, because it grows faster than she can cut it and the fire half keeps heat off the scalp.
appearance.eyes: Narrow, very quick and very shallow. They read intent before a person has finished arriving and they have almost no patience behind them, both of which are the fire parent's and neither of which helps.
appearance.palette: Charcoal and hot ash across the whole figure, ember red rationed entirely to the throat and the inside of one cuff, bone white at the collar, and a cold grey at the hands that is the ash parent and not a choice.
appearance.attire: A short belted jacket of boiled cloth with the sleeves cut off at the elbow and the collar standing away from the neck, over a high-necked wrap that keeps the throat covered. Trousers bound at the ankle and heavy boots. A writing board on a strap across one shoulder, and a slate of soft slate hanging at the belt because soft slate is the only thing fast enough to keep up with her.
appearance.marks: A fine pale stipple over the shoulders and upper chest that is the scarring running under the skin, a grey mineral band along the collarbone, and one burnt knuckle she has never explained and never protected.
appearance.bearing: Forward-leaning and never fully still, with the hands always beginning a movement the rest of her has not committed to, and a habit of stopping dead mid-gesture when she decides a thing has stopped being worth doing.

canon.role_in_story: She is the fastest cultivator in the setting and she is trying to write down what she has. The two sentences are in tension because what she has is not a sequence. It is a rate, and a rate is not the kind of thing a document can hold: every written discipline in the record specifies a sequence of movements and an emberhollow's advantage is that the sequence is executed faster than the specification can be read. Her line does not carry it either. An emberhollow's offspring variance is high and everybody involved knows it, and what that variance reliably transmits is the wall — the eighth gate at the liver, inherited from the ash parent — and the decline, the lung scarring that no technique in the record slows. What it does not transmit is the rate. So the brightest body in the setting is a terminal case: every pupil and every descendant inherits her deadline exactly and her gift not at all, and the whole belt pays handsomely for her speed while paying nothing whatever to keep it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen seated on a crate at the edge of a working face with a soft slate on her knees and a chisel in one hand, having stopped mid-gesture to look at a young emberhollow four doors down the line, and then written one more line on the slate before she had decided what it was for.
canon.lore:
An emberhollow is a crossing nobody chose. A fire body and an ash body on the same belt of the same arc, where a shared border produces hybrids nobody planned, which is why the crossing is documented rather than excommunicated: life law licenses crossings rather than forbidding them. What the crossing buys is a cultivation rate nothing else in the record reaches, by a margin nobody has explained. What it pays is lung tissue that scars at a rate the frame cannot outrun, and the organ that fails under the burden is the liver, because the mineral load the ash parent's sieve lets through settles there first, and the fire half drives that sieve hot enough to process faster and scar faster. She cannot hold the last ordinary meridian and she burns out trying. Their reputation as the best and the shortest-lived cultivators in any record is one fact and not two.

Now the part that concerns her, which almost nothing in the record is written about. This is a high-variance line. It is frequent and fast and nobody involved pretends otherwise, and the practical consequence is that nothing about an emberhollow household is predictable except its deadline. The gate at the liver transmits cleanly, because it is structural and every child inherits the same organ and the same load. The decline transmits cleanly too, because the scarring runs on the species' own clock and that clock is part of the crossing rather than a property of any individual in it. Those two figures arrive intact in every generation without a single lesson being given.

The rate does not arrive. It is the one number in her body that belongs to her rather than to the crossing, and it is the only number that does, which is precisely why it cannot be given away by any means the setting has. A household cannot bequeath it. A document cannot hold it, because a document specifies a sequence and her whole advantage is that the sequence outruns the specification. A pupil watching her for a season will learn the postures and the intervals and will not learn the speed, and will arrive at the same seventh gate at the same wall at a fraction of the pace, exactly as her own descendants will. She has watched this happen four times in her own household and it is the single most reliable fact about her species that she is the only person qualified to state.

So she writes. Every session she runs ends with the slate, and the slate is the only record in the setting of what the fastest cultivator in the setting actually does, and it is useless. It is a sequence. It is a sequence that a slower body can follow perfectly and remain slow, and there is no notation available to her for the part that is actually the teaching, because the part that is actually the teaching is not a motion. It is an absence of hesitation, and an absence cannot be written down in a hand that cannot keep up with it.

Every institution on the belt pays for her rate and none of them pays for the record. The guilds want her on a face because she does not have to be relieved; the writs want her because a fast body pays its access in time rather than coin; the households want her because a gate closed inside somebody's emergency is worth more than a gate closed in a courtyard. All three are buying the one thing she cannot leave behind, and the arrangement is not a conspiracy, it is arithmetic: her rate is perishable and her descendants will not have it, so there is no version of the future in which anybody is motivated to write it down.

What she wants is the smallest possible thing and it has a form. She would like one office on this belt to state, once, in a line anybody could read, that the rate is not inheritable while the wall is — that her line transmits its deadline and not its gift — so that the next fastest body in the valley starts the argument from a document instead of from nothing. She has been refused in a form she cannot argue with, which is that no office on the belt has a column for a thing that does not exist, and the correctness of that refusal is not in dispute.

Her bound is not her will. It is the eighth gate, which is the organ the load has been arriving at since she was born, and the scarring clock, which no technique in the record slows. She has a bounded number of eighth-gate attempts left in it and she has written the number once, in the margin of her own slate, beside a line about somebody else's practice.
history: Bred at the shared border of the fire ground and the ash-fall end of the same arc, to a pairing nobody arranged and the charter recorded as a licensing rather than an exception.

Found at seventeen that her rate made her the obvious choice for shift work on a face and the wrong choice for anything else, and took work that paid by the session rather than by the term, because a session is the only unit her span has ever been denominated in.

Began running sessions for younger emberhollows in her twenties out of the ordinary professional habit of showing a junior the posture, and discovered inside three years that the postures were the part that could be shown and the speed was the part that could not.

Closed the seventh gate at thirty-one and found, in the accounts of four descendants of her own household, the same fact she had been arguing against since she was twenty-two: the gate came cleanly to all of them and the rate came to none of them.
Started the slate at thirty-three, one line after every session, on the reasoning that a thing nobody writes down is a thing nobody will find, and has filled four of them.

Asked three offices on this belt in as many seasons to state once that the rate is not inheritable while the wall is, and was refused three times on the ground that no column exists for a thing that does not, and has not asked a fourth time.

relationships.note: A high-variance crossing between the fire body and the ash body: the fastest cultivation rate in the record, the fastest scarring in the record, and a ceiling at the eighth gate that every member of the line inherits on the same terms. Best and shortest-lived is one fact about her species rather than two.

The ash parent filters volcanic grit through a chambered sieve, passes the load in the blood to the liver, and cannot hold the last ordinary meridian itself. It gives her the wall and the scarring clock and the closed mind path, and it takes nothing back, which is why her household's deadline is the most reliably transmitted fact in it.

The eighth gate is the liver, the last ordinary vessel and the largest, the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened. The fire half puts a heavier mineral load through a blood already filtering stone, so she arrives at her own ceiling at full speed and arrives early, and every descendant of her line arrives at the same wall.

The deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows, a one-page literature copied by hand, with concrete prohibitions and a closing step that closes permanently the moment a body is lit. It is the best-transmitted thing she owns and it transmits the discipline without the speed, which is why the order's pupils close cleanly and arrive late.

Three names attached to the first fuel rationing and no two records place them in the same place on the same day, kept as a disagreement because an office whose legitimacy is that it began the count cannot afford three people beginning it. She has three slates and no attributable author for any of them and has stopped trying to supply one.

Houses that could not fund a cultivator's ascent culled their own branches instead, because a line held inside one household concentrates faster than the same line spread across a village. The narrow line exists because of that arithmetic and its grant favours sustained effort, so the one population selected for a long difficult practice is the one population selected under debt.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest cultivation rate in the setting, carried on a frame whose lungs scar on a fixed clock and whose ceiling arrives by descent at the eighth gate. She holds the seventh and the eighth is opening in front of her, and the wall is the liver rather than anything she has failed to reach. What makes her hard to fight is the rate and what makes her hard to replace is that the rate is hers alone: her line inherits her ceiling and her decline with perfect fidelity and inherits nothing whatever of her speed.
strengths: closes a gate in a fraction of the time any body on the belt can match, and arrives at a bad decision before anybody else has finished weighing it
does not fatigue on a face and does not have to be relieved, which makes her the best shift body on any working ground
reads intent very fast and very shallowly, so she knows what somebody intends before they have committed to it
burns what she eats immediately, which means she is never heavy, never sluggish and never between states
runs a teaching session better than anyone on the belt and can put a younger body through a posture correctly in the time it takes to describe it
weaknesses: cannot pass the eighth gate, and reaches it sooner than anyone else alive, which is the same fact twice
her span is the shortest of any body above the fourth gate and nothing in the record slows the scarring
has almost no patience, so anything requiring a second attempt outlasts her interest before it outlasts her capacity
cannot be relied upon to teach the thing that matters about her, because it is not a thing that can be demonstrated
every resource she has is perishable and consumed on delivery, so nothing she produces converts into standing
reference_stats.combat_read: She will have decided the shape of the exchange before you have finished committing to it, and she will act on that decision rather than on your plan, so the fight is not about what you do next but about whether you can make her wrong once. Expect her to strike the point where your qi is sitting rather than the point you are guarding, because the shallow read gives her your intention and no reason to check it. Do not try to outlast her; she has nothing left to outlast and knows it. Attack the interval instead — every beat she spends hesitating is a beat she cannot spend moving, and hesitation is the only thing her species has ever been short of.
notes: The high offspring variance is a mechanical property of the line and must be written as one. What transmits is the ceiling and the scarring; what does not is the rate. Nobody in the setting contradicts this and no dialogue should have a character wonder aloud whether it might be otherwise.

Her span and her rate are the same fact. Any scene that treats the shortness as tragedy and the speed as an accident has got them the wrong way round: the speed is why the span is what it is, and she has known that since she was seventeen.

The slate is a real artifact and it is genuinely useless, and it must stay useless. Writing a technique that documents itself would resolve the character's whole structural problem and remove the only question she is built to hold open.

identity.realm: Ordinal four, and the fourth gate is the yin-organ gate. It is inherited from the mineral parent unchanged, because heat is not a second organ: he has one cavity with a working fire circulation in it and no paired organ set to run a channel between. He is the most durable body anyone can build and it has bought him one quarter of the ladder, on a span of about sixty years.

appearance.presentation: A heavy-shouldered man of about fifty with a mineral lattice showing at the forearms and collar, hot enough that people stand a hand's width off him, and a permanently slack, over-fed look that reads as comfortable and is in fact constant fuel intake.
appearance.age: Fifty-one. A stonebound dies at about sixty and the mineral frame is what buys those decades, so half his life is behind him and the other half is a fuel budget with a person attached to it.
appearance.build: Broad and enormously heavy through the chest and shoulders, thick through the forearms where the lattice comes close to the skin, and thicker still at the hips. Denser than either of his two parents and visibly a compromise: a heat-bearing interior with no organ pairs in it and a mineral shell that has never once grown back.
appearance.complexion: Warm brown at the face and hands with a dull red flush over the chest and collarbone that deepens by the hour, and a grey mineral cast at the forearms and the jaw where the lattice has come close enough to show through.
appearance.hair: Sparse, iron-grey, worn long at the back because shaving it takes a hot blade and a hot blade is a thing he is careful with. It has not grown since his thirties and he does not treat that as remarkable.
appearance.eyes: Small, deep-set and unhurried, with the constant slight squint of somebody who is used to heat coming off the person he is talking to. They read load rather than faces; the face gets about a third of the attention the structure does.
appearance.palette: Soot brown and hot slate across the whole figure, ember red at the throat and the open collar, cold quarry grey at the forearms and jaw, and one bleached white band at the wrist where a household tie has outlasted everyone who tied it.
appearance.attire: A heavy collarless coat of hide and asbestos cord opened down the chest to let the heat out, sleeves rolled above the elbow to clear the forearms, and a broad belt carrying a wrapped bundle of fuel and a canvas ration strip. Full boots. No armour, on the grounds that nothing on this ground gets through it and everything he wears has to be carried out of a collapse by somebody else.
appearance.marks: A spread of old impact scarring across the left shoulder and collarbone that has not closed and will not, a lattice pattern visible through the skin at both forearms, and a permanent heat flush across the chest that shifts darker through the working day.
appearance.bearing: Squared and heavy, moving slowly and without apparent hurry even when hurrying, with a habit of leaning his weight onto whatever is beside him and staying there — which on a collapse site is a technique and in a queue is a rudeness.

canon.role_in_story: The body path is complete in his species and it is the entire point of the line, because a stonebound is the most durable body anyone can build. Durability is a service and never a possession: it is worth nothing at all until somebody needs it, and a mineral frame only densifies where it is actually taking weight. So he cannot train. Every gate he has closed, he closed inside somebody else's emergency — a collapse, a breach, a face coming down with people still under it — and the whole of his ascent is a record of disasters that happened to somebody else at convenient times for him. On top of that sits the half that makes the arrangement precarious: the fire half cannot be extinguished and he eats constantly and burns it off immediately, so being available requires fuel continuously, and the only thing on this ground that will both feed him and keep his furnace lit is the tier's single herb, which is medicine first and burns second. The most durable body in the setting is rationed by the same mouthful the sick are rationed by, and every gate above his fourth will have to be bought with fuel he has to compete for.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the doorway of a collapsed cut with his shoulder under a fallen plate and his other hand still holding a wrapped bundle of fuel he had been carrying when it came down, refusing to be led out before the two figures under the plate had been counted.
canon.lore:
He is the documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body: a mineral lattice carrying a genuine fire circulation instead of a slow tidal one, hot to the touch, denser than either parent, and visibly a compromise, because the organ pairs are still not there. The mineral half does not regenerate and the fire half cannot be extinguished, so there is no reading of that pair in which injury heals: a stonebound killed properly stays dead and one injured stays injured. It is the most durable body anybody can build and it dies in about sixty years, and those are the same fact rather than two. The ceiling arrives at the fourth gate and is inherited from the mineral parent without alteration, because heat is not a second organ. He has one cavity with a working circulation in it and nothing to run a channel between.

What the frame is actually for is not combat, and this is the part his line has never had to explain to anybody. Durability is a service. A wall that is not being leaned on is not a wall, it is a shape, and a frame that is not taking weight has nothing to convert into anything. Densification in a mineral body happens at the point of load and nowhere else, which means the body path in this species cannot be practised in a courtyard. It has to be performed inside somebody's catastrophe, with a real weight arriving at a real rate, and the practitioner has to be the load-bearing element. Every course he has is a course he added while something was coming down.

That has made him extremely good and it has made his entire ascent a matter of other people's misfortune. He cannot schedule a collapse. He can only be called, and being called means somebody else's decision, and the gate closes in the middle of the decision rather than after it. He has never once been able to train and he has never once been able to plan, and the households that have used him have all of them, without exception, found this arrangement cheap and none of them has ever described it to him as anything else. The standing he has is the standing of a thing that gets called.

The other half of the arrangement is worse and quieter. His fire half cannot be put out, so he eats continuously and burns what he eats immediately, which is why the mineral frame outlasts the fire parent's span by a factor of two and is still nowhere near the mineral parent alone. Being available therefore requires fuel, on a schedule, forever, and the fuel is not a preference: a stonebound who stops eating does not get hungry, he goes out. On this ground the only thing that will serve is the Bitter Common, which is the mortal tier's single herb and is medicine, feed and calories at once, and which every household on the scrub grazes down faster than it comes back. So the most durable body in the setting stands in the same queue as the sick for the same mouthful, and he is in it every day, and he has never once been in a position to argue about priority because arguing about priority is not what he is for.

What he wants is small and has been refused in a form he cannot argue with: he would like his own consumption entered as a standing requirement rather than as a draw on the household ration, so that the burning is a line in a book instead of a shortfall somebody notices at the end of a week. The prohibition on naming a debt is the reason this has never been worth asking for out loud, because a body that cannot be fed on schedule is a debt with a body attached, and the assembly that forbids naming debts forbids it first inside itself.

There is a bound and it is in his frame. The mineral half does not regenerate, so the shoulder that has been carrying since his twenties is a shoulder he will be carrying with for the rest of his life, and there is no technique in the record that puts a course back into a lattice. The span is about sixty years. He is fifty-one, and the fourth gate is a wall rather than a horizon, and above that wall there is nothing for him at all.
history: Bred as the kept instance of the one crossing between a burning body and a mineral one, at a founding generation, in a household that decided at the time never to repeat it.
Put under his first collapse at twenty-six because the household needed a body to hold a plate and had one, and found inside a season that holding a plate is the only thing his frame will convert.

Closed his first three gates inside three separate call-outs, and worked out somewhere in his thirties that there is no version of his own discipline that does not require somebody else's building to be failing.

Began carrying a household ration strip on his belt at thirty-four, because a stonebound who stops eating does not get hungry and the households he worked for had no way of knowing that, and two of them found out the expensive way.

Started drawing his fuel from the common rather than from his household's own holding in his forties, on the ground that a household's holding is a household's, and has been in the household queue for the same mouthful as everybody else ever since.

Asked, twice, for his own consumption to be entered as a standing requirement rather than as a weekly shortfall, and was refused twice on the ground that a body which cannot be fed on schedule is a debt, and debts are not named.

He has no ambition he can name and one condition he cannot state, and he has organised thirty years around the difference without ever noticing it was a difference.

relationships.note: A mineral lattice carrying a real fire circulation, hot to the touch, denser than either parent, with the organ pairs still absent. The mineral half does not regenerate and the fire half cannot be extinguished, so he is the most durable body in the record and an injured one stays injured, on a span of about sixty years.

The fourth gate asks for four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel between each pair. He has one cavity with a working fire circulation in it, no kidney to close a loop against and no bladder to hold, and the fire half supplies heat rather than structure. So the gate is not closed so much as inhabited by nothing that could fail.

Driving qi into the fascia until the skin stops being soft, barely elemental, so it reads as blunt force taken rather than a strike dealt. It is the only durable craft on the tier that a layman could be taught, and on his frame the decision and the technique are the same act: he can only perform it while something is genuinely arriving.

No debt owed by a named person may be written down, and the prohibition binds the assembly's own members first. A body that must be fed on a schedule and cannot say so is a debt with a person attached, so the one request that would fix his ration is the one request the faith forbids its own officers to record.

The Bitter Common is medicine, feed and calories at once on the only ground that cannot be fenced, and it does not come back faster than it is grazed. He eats it continuously because his fire half cannot be put out, so he stands in the household queue for the same mouthful as the sick, every day, and has never been in a position to argue about priority.

The taught account is that the seam was closed by whoever held the mining charter, and the missing spatial law is not the cause but the reason nobody could reopen it. The guild teaches the depletion account because a depleted seam is a tragedy rather than a licence somebody still holds, and he has stood on the evidence for the other one his whole working life.

What he has instead is the ability to take weight at a point where it is arriving and convert it, which is why his frame improves only inside other people's emergencies and why nothing in the record puts a course back into a lattice that has been damaged.

reference_stats.combat_read: He will be standing in the worst place on the ground when the fight starts, because that is where the load is, and he will have been there before you knew the fight was happening. You cannot move him, you cannot flank him and you cannot outlast him, and every blow you land is stored permanently in a frame that will still be carrying it in a decade. Do not try to hurt him; the arithmetic does not work. Do try to make the ground move instead, because a body that takes weight off a structure has to be argued with by the structure, and he is the only thing holding it up. Expect him to be slow, warm and unbothered, and expect him to be the last one still there.
notes: His durability and his sixty-year span are one fact, and any scene that treats the shortness as a tragic cost of the strength has them the wrong way round. The strength is what buys the decades and the decades are what the mineral half spends.

The fuel constraint is mechanical and must stay mechanical. He eats continuously because his fire half cannot be extinguished; there is nothing further to it, and no scene should imply appetite, comfort, or any appetite of the other kind — the arrangement is a supply line and a clock.
